skill.name: google-trends-interest-and-related-query-scraper
skill.description: Retrieve public Google Trends interest, regional breakdowns, related queries, and trending topics through an Apify Actor, with comparison for up to five terms.
skill.summary: Export Google Trends data through Apify for keyword comparisons, regional research, and trending topic monitoring.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

No evidence found of prompt injection or unauthorized exfiltration; remote Actor implementation and runtime behavior were not audited.

content.user_title: Analyze Google Trends Interest and Related Queries
content.value_statement: Manual Google Trends exports make repeated keyword and regional comparisons time-consuming. This skill submits configured requests to an Apify Actor and retrieves structured results.
actual_capabilities: Request interest over time, interest by region, related topics, and related queries through the documented Apify Actor.
Configure comparison mode for up to five search terms on a shared 0-100 scale.
Filter requests by location, time window, custom dates, Google category, search surface, and geographic resolution.
Request Trending Now results with lookback windows, category filters, and optional matching news links.
Run the supplied Node CLI with inline JSON or a selected input file and print dataset results as JSON.
Use documented curl examples to start asynchronous runs, check status, and retrieve dataset items.
limitations: Requires internet access, an Apify account, and APIFY_TOKEN; Actor usage is billed by Apify.
The scraper runs remotely on Apify; the supplied files do not include or verify its implementation.
The Node runner requires Node 18 or later and uses a synchronous endpoint with a documented 300-second wait limit.
Only public data is supported; comparison mode accepts at most five terms, and news enrichment covers only matching highlighted stories.

use_cases.title: Compare Keyword Interest
use_cases.description: Compare up to five campaign keywords for one location and time window using the same interest scale.

use_cases.title: Study Regional Demand
use_cases.description: Retrieve regional interest and related queries for product categories to support market research.

use_cases.title: Monitor Trending Topics
use_cases.description: Retrieve country-level Trending Now items and available news links for editorial research.

prompt_templates.title: Explore One Keyword
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve Google Trends interest and related queries for [keyword] in [country] over the past three months. Limit the run to 10 records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a small initial interest request.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Search Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [term one], [term two], and [term three] in [country] over the past year. Enable compareMode and summarize the shared-scale results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare multiple terms with consistent filters.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve Trending Now items in [country] from the past 24 hours. Include matching news links, limit results to 20, and summarize notable topics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect current topics with optional news enrichment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Regional Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure [keyword] for [country], [start date] through [end date], and YouTube Search. Request regional breakdowns and related queries. Confirm costs before starting asynchronously.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine custom dates, surface filters, regional analysis, and asynchronous execution.

output_examples.input: Compare three keywords in the United States over the past year.
output: Illustrative report layout, not a live result.
Scope: three terms, United States, past year, comparison mode enabled.
Comparison: returned interest series and per-term regional or related-query data, where available.
Source: Google Trends Explore link supplied in the dataset.

output_examples.input: Retrieve current trending topics in Canada with available news links.
output: Illustrative report layout, not a live result.
Scope: Canada, Trending Now, past 24 hours.
Topic details: title, rank, volume text, and growth percentage where returned.
News: matching headline, source, and link where enrichment is available.

best_practices: Start with a small maxItems value, confirm current Actor pricing, and inspect returned records before increasing volume.
Use identical location, time, category, and search surface settings for comparisons; enable compareMode for a shared scale.
Keep APIFY_TOKEN in the environment and submit only intended public research inputs, without cookies or private account data.
anti_patterns: Treating the default runner as a local scraper that works without an Apify account or internet access.
Comparing independently normalized interest values as though they share one common scale.
Assuming the provided asynchronous example guarantees completion after one status check; verify completion before exporting the full dataset.

faq.question: Do I need an Apify account?
faq.answer: Yes. Set APIFY_TOKEN before running requests. Apify bills Actor usage to your account according to current pricing.

faq.question: Does the scraper run on my computer?
faq.answer: No. The local runner reads your selected input and submits it to an Apify Actor. The scraping executes remotely.

faq.question: How many terms can I compare?
faq.answer: Comparison mode supports up to five terms on a shared 0-100 scale. Without comparison mode, terms are scraped independently.

faq.question: Which Google search surfaces are supported?
faq.answer: The input schema lists Web Search, Image Search, News Search, Google Shopping, and YouTube Search.

faq.question: Can I export CSV directly with the Node runner?
faq.answer: The supplied runner prints JSON only. CSV requires a separate conversion or export step.

faq.question: What should I do when a run takes too long?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous API flow for large runs. Check run completion before retrieving the dataset; the Node runner has no asynchronous mode.
